name: Complement cascade
summary: Three ways in, one way out. Classical: C1 binds IgG or IgM on antigen. Lectin: mannose-binding lectin with its MASPs binds microbial sugars. Both cut C4 and C2 (C4a, C2a released) and C4b + C2b make the C3 convertase C4b2b. Alternative: C3 breaks down on its own; C3b on a microbe binds factor B, factor D cuts it, and C3bBb (stabilized by properdin) is the C3 convertase. Both convertases cut C3: C3a is an anaphylatoxin, C3b an opsonin that also joins each convertase to make the C5 convertases (and feeds the alternative pathway: amplification). C5 → C5a (anaphylatoxin, draws neutrophils) + C5b, which with C6–C9 forms the membrane attack complex (lyses Neisseria). Regulators: C1 esterase inhibitor (hereditary angioedema), DAF/CD55 and CD59 (PNH), factor H and factor I.
tissue: blood plasma and tissue fluid (made mostly in the liver)

c4.name: C4
c4.notes: Cut by C1s (classical) or MASP-2 (lectin). Low C4 with normal C3: C1 inhibitor deficiency (hereditary angioedema) between attacks is low C4 too.

c2.name: C2
c2.notes: Cut by C1s or MASP-2. C2 deficiency is the most common inherited complement deficiency (SLE-like disease).

c4b.name: C4b
c4b.notes: The larger piece; binds the microbial surface next to the antibody or lectin, then takes up C2b.

c2b.name: C2b
c2b.notes: The larger piece of C2 (it used to be called C2a, so older books write the convertase C4b2a).

c4b2a.name: C4b2b
c4b2a.notes: The C3 convertase of the classical and lectin pathways. Decay-accelerating factor (DAF, CD55) takes it apart; C4-binding protein too.

c3alt.name: C3
c3alt.notes: In plasma, C3 breaks down slowly on its own (“tickover”). The C3b it gives sticks to whatever surface is nearest: on our cells regulators (factor H, factor I, DAF) remove it; on microbes it stays and starts the alternative pathway.

c3balt.name: C3b
c3balt.notes: C3b from tickover, stuck to a microbial surface. C3b made by any pathway does the same thing here: the amplification loop.

fb.name: Factor B
fb.notes: Binds C3b, then factor D cuts it into Bb (stays: the convertase) and Ba (released).

c3bbb.name: C3bBb
c3bbb.notes: The alternative pathway’s C3 convertase; properdin stabilizes it. DAF and factor H take it apart. Every C3b it makes can form another one: the amplification loop.

c3.name: C3
c3.notes: The most abundant complement protein; where all three pathways meet. Low C3: post-streptococcal glomerulonephritis, membranoproliferative GN, SLE (with low C4). C3 deficiency: severe recurrent pyogenic infections (sinus, lung) and immune-complex disease.

c3b.name: C3b
c3b.notes: The opsonin (with IgG): phagocytes bind it through CR1. It also clears immune complexes and joins each C3 convertase to make a C5 convertase. Factor I (with factor H) cuts it to iC3b.

c4b2a3b.name: C4b2b3b
c4b2a3b.notes: The classical and lectin C5 convertase.

c5.name: C5
c5.notes: Cut by either C5 convertase. Eculizumab and ravulizumab block it (PNH, atypical HUS, myasthenia gravis), so vaccinate against meningococcus first.

c5b.name: C5b
c5b.notes: Starts the membrane attack complex on the surface.

mac.name: Membrane attack complex (C5b–9)
mac.notes: A pore of C5b, C6, C7, C8 and many C9s that lyses the cell; matters most against Neisseria (thin cell wall). CD59 (and DAF) protect our own cells: both missing in PNH (no GPI anchor, PIGA mutation).

c1.name: C1 (C1q, C1r, C1s)
c1.notes: Classical pathway. C1q binds the Fc of IgM or IgG bound to antigen (“GM makes classic cars”: IgG and IgM fix complement); C1r activates C1s, which cuts C4 and C2. C1 esterase inhibitor shuts it off: deficiency (or ACE inhibitors, which add bradykinin) causes hereditary angioedema.

masp.name: MBL–MASP
masp.notes: Lectin pathway. Mannose-binding lectin binds mannose and other sugars on microbial surfaces (no antibody needed); its MASPs (like C1r and C1s) cut C4 and C2.

tick.name: Spontaneous hydrolysis
tick.notes: The alternative pathway needs no antibody or lectin: C3 breaks down slowly all the time, and C3b that lands on a microbe (no regulators there) is not removed.

join_c2b.name: C4b binds C2b
join_c2b.notes: C4b on the surface takes up C2b to make the classical and lectin C3 convertase.

fd.name: Factor D
fd.notes: Cuts factor B once it is bound to C3b: Bb stays (C3bBb), Ba is released. Properdin then stabilizes C3bBb.

c3conv_cl.name: C3 convertase (C4b2b)
c3conv_cl.notes: The classical and lectin C3 convertase.

addc3b_cl.name: C3b joins C4b2b
addc3b_cl.notes: A C3b next to the C3 convertase turns it into a C5 convertase.

addc3b_alt.name: C3b joins C3bBb
addc3b_alt.notes: A second C3b turns C3bBb into a C5 convertase.

c5conv_cl.name: C5 convertase (C4b2b3b)
c5conv_cl.notes: The classical and lectin C5 convertase.

mac_asm.name: MAC assembly (C6–C9)
mac_asm.notes: C6, C7, C8, then many C9s add to C5b and insert into the membrane. C5–C9 deficiency: recurrent Neisseria (meningococcal, gonococcal) infections.

drugs.name: Eculizumab
drugs.note: Antibody against C5: no C5 cleavage, no MAC. PNH, atypical HUS; vaccinate against Neisseria first.

drugs.name: Eculizumab
drugs.note: Antibody against C5: no C5 cleavage, no MAC. PNH, atypical HUS; vaccinate against Neisseria first.

groups.name: Classical and lectin pathways
groups.notes: Classical: C1 bound to IgG or IgM on antigen (“GM makes classic cars”). Lectin: mannose-binding lectin on microbial sugars. Both cut C4 and C2 to make C4b2b.

groups.name: Alternative pathway
groups.notes: Spontaneous C3 breakdown on microbial surfaces; factor B and factor D; properdin stabilizes C3bBb. Also amplifies the other two: C3b from any pathway feeds it.

groups.name: Common pathway
groups.notes: All three pathways meet at C3: C3a (anaphylatoxin) and C3b (opsonin, and the third piece of each C5 convertase).

groups.name: Terminal pathway
groups.notes: C5b joins C6–C9 to form the membrane attack complex. C5–C9 deficiency: recurrent Neisseria infections. Eculizumab blocks C5.
